results.title: How to Prepare Rose Bushes for Winter: What to Protect and When
results.description:
How do you prepare rose bushes for winter without damaging healthy growth? Winter rose care depends on the type of rose, your local climate, and whether the plant grows in the ground or in a container.

**Read the full Garden Insider guide:**
https://gardeninsider.org/plants/flowers/how-to-prepare-a-rose-bush-for-winter/

In this video, you'll learn how to winterize rose bushes, protect vulnerable roots and graft unions, and avoid common mistakes with pruning, mulching, and winter covers.

Topics covered:

- How to prepare rose bushes for winter
- Which roses need winter protection
- Hardy shrub roses vs tender hybrid teas
- Why the graft union needs special attention
- When to stop fertilizing and encouraging new growth
- Why heavy fall pruning can damage next season's flowering potential
- How to remove diseased foliage before winter
- When to water roses before the ground freezes
- When to apply winter protection
- How to mound soil around vulnerable rose crowns
- Why mulch depth depends on rose type and climate
- How to protect climbing rose canes
- Why sealing roses under plastic can cause problems
- How to overwinter potted roses
- How to monitor moisture during winter dormancy
- When and how to remove winter protection in spring

Not every rose needs heavy winter protection. Some established hardy shrub roses require little intervention, while tender grafted roses and container-grown plants may need additional insulation.

Timing matters. Covering roses too early can trap moisture and interfere with dormancy, while unnecessary pruning may remove healthy canes needed for future flowers.

Learn how to choose a winter protection method that matches your rose variety and growing conditions.

results.title: Proper Winter Pruning of Floribunda Roses in Southern California
results.description:
Winter is the most important pruning season for roses in Southern California. In this video, I discuss how to properly prune floribunda roses during our mild winter climate to encourage strong spring growth and abundant blooms.

You’ll see the full process step-by-step:
• Cutting plants back to knee height
• Removing dead, diseased, damaged, and crossing canes
• Pruning to outward-facing buds for better structure
• Removing persistent leaves to reduce disease pressure
• Cleaning up debris for improved plant health

Because Southern California winters are mild, roses don’t always fully go dormant, which makes proper winter pruning and sanitation especially important for preventing black spot and other fungal diseases.

This method works well for floribundas and many hybrid teas grown in USDA Zones 9–10.

If you garden in Southern California, this winter pruning technique will help you reset plant structure, improve airflow, and maximize your spring bloom flush.

results.title: The AMISH Way to Care for Desert Rose in Winter — The Secret to Healthy Growth Next Season
results.description:
👉 Want to learn how to live a simpler, more independent life? Take a deeper look here: https://independentbackyard.com/my-book/#aff=natanaelfernamdes


Sixty-five degrees. That's the temperature where a Desert Rose's growth quietly shuts down, long before any frost warning ever reaches your phone. I am Elias Yoder, and today I'm giving you the exact winter protocol for Adenium obesum — and why treating it like any other cold-hardy succulent is exactly how so many of them are lost every year.

I farm in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania. This plant has almost no margin for error around cold, even while it stays remarkably forgiving of nearly everything else. Today's video covers tracking overnight lows instead of daytime highs, deliberately choosing between a real winter rest or genuine active growth, cutting watering down to a fraction of summer levels, checking whether your plant is grafted, never risking an actual freeze, waiting until spring to prune cold damage, keeping even a dormant plant in real light, and reintroducing outdoor sun gradually in spring.

results.title: Stop "Keeping Plants Warm": The Real Secret to Winter Survival
results.description:
Winter doesn’t ask for permission. It arrives with killing frosts and desiccating winds that can either strengthen your garden or destroy it entirely. Most gardeners think winter protection is about keeping plants warm—but that's a mistake that could cost you your entire landscape.

In this video, we dive into the documented techniques and horticultural science behind overwintering success. Whether you are protecting tender roses, young fruit trees, or trying to harvest root vegetables in January, these methods ensure your garden emerges vibrant and healthy when the snow finally melts.

Key Strategies for a Resilient Garden
The "Mulch Donut": Always leave a 2-inch gap between your mulch and the plant stem to prevent rot and fungal disease.

Container Survival: Remember that potted plants are hardy to about two zones warmer than their rating; move them to a shed or bury the pots in-ground.

The Power of Snow: Eight inches of snow can act as a natural insulator, keeping soil temperatures at a stable 32°F regardless of the air temperature.

Overwintering Veggies: Carrots and leeks can be harvested all winter if kept under 12 inches of straw and a weighted tarp.

Anti-Desiccant Sprays: Research from Cornell University shows these can reduce moisture loss by up to 80% in evergreens.

"Winter protection isn't about fighting nature. It's about working with natural processes to minimize the stresses that damage plants."

0:00 - The Great Winter Test

If you love dahlias but you do not have garden space, this video is for you. You can absolutely grow dahlias in pots and containers, but most people run into the same avoidable problems like weak plants, broken stems, rot, and yellow leaves. In this video, I walk you through the exact setup and routine that keeps potted dahlias strong, upright, and blooming.

What you will learn in this video
-How to choose the right pot size so plants do not tip over and so the soil holds enough nutrients
-How to set up drainage correctly so tubers do not sit in water and rot
-What potting soil to use and what to mix in before planting
-How deep to plant tubers in a pot and the clean, easy way to do it
-Why staking at planting time matters and where to place the stake
-The biggest watering mistake with potted dahlias and how to avoid it
